title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. College weekend review: Tuesday through Saturday (Oct. 20-24), graded. Then next college weekend.

paragraphs: Every pick below is graded against the line printed on its card when the game kicked off, not the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss.

What got graded: all 56 college games from Tuesday, Oct. 20 through Saturday, Oct. 24. Each recap starts with the card, then rides along with the tickets: the number each side and the total needed, the plays and flags that swung them, then who called it and who missed it. Play detail comes from ESPN's official play-by-play.

Card line: Florida International −10.5, total 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had Florida International −10.5 and the Under, projecting Florida International 28, Middle Tennessee 16. Final: Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23. Middle Tennessee won by 3, and the teams scored 49 points.

Laying 10.5 with Florida International meant you needed an 11-point win, and the best the Panthers ever gave you was an 8-0 lead in the first quarter. Middle Tennessee led 13-8 at halftime and never gave you another look. The −10.5 ticket went in the drawer with 2:06 left in the third, when Terrence Brown broke a 54-yard touchdown run for a 23-16 Middle Tennessee lead. Dominic Bourgeois then added his fourth field goal, a 28-yarder, for 26-16, and Middle Tennessee +10.5 holders could start thinking about breakfast. Florida International even had a 46-yard try blocked on the last play of the first half, which is the kind of night it was for that side.

The over 45.5 was a slow burn. After Bourgeois's kick the game sat at 42 points, 3.5 short, with ten minutes to play. Then JJ Kohl found Sterling Joseph for a 21-yard touchdown with 6:06 left, and that made it 26-23 and 49 points, over the 45.5. Under holders watched Middle Tennessee kneel it out at 0:49 and 0:33 knowing it was already too late. Florida International at −10.5 asked a lot, and Middle Tennessee didn't go along with it.
Called it: The Formula and In The Trenches on Middle Tennessee +10.5, covered by 13.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Over 45.5, cleared it by 3.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Florida International −10.5, missed by 13.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Under 45.5, went over by 3.5 points.
Follow The Money: no pick.

Card line: Delaware −3, total 52.5. The Cover Writer's card had Delaware −3 and the Over, projecting Delaware 29, Missouri State 24. Final: Missouri State 38, Delaware 61. Delaware won by 23, and the teams scored 99 points.

Delaware −3 holders spent the first half wishing they had the other side. Missouri State took a 28-24 lead into the break on Henry Belin IV's 6-yard touchdown pass with 14 seconds left, and it was still a one-score game at 38-35 Delaware midway through the third. Then the turnovers started falling the right way. Brandon Gorham recovered a fumble on a Jawarren Corbin sack of Belin, and Nick Minicucci ran in from a yard out at 4:01 for a 45-35 lead. George Mullins and Corbin then picked off Belin on either side of a Jo Silver touchdown run that made it 52-35. By the fourth quarter the −3 was a memory, the good kind.

The over 52.5 was the easiest ticket on the board. The teams had 52 at halftime, half a point short, and Silver's 12-yard touchdown catch at 12:53 of the third made it 59. The final landed at 99. Anyone holding the under was half a point from trouble at the break, and the trouble showed up with 46.5 points of company.

Card line: South Alabama −3, total 64.5. The Cover Writer's card had Marshall +3 and the Over, projecting South Alabama 34, Marshall 32. Final: South Alabama 13, Marshall 20. Marshall won by 7, and the teams scored 33 points.

South Alabama −3 needed a field goal and a hook, and for most of the night nobody was scoring enough to settle anything. PJ Martin's 19-yard touchdown run with 4:38 left tied it 13-13, and the Jaguars ticket was alive. Moments later Marshall broke a 75-yard Zion Turner touchdown run, and a Marshall holding flag brought it all the way back. Judah Price ran in from 5 yards out with 1:49 left for a 20-13 Marshall lead, and Jared Hollins' fourth-down pass fell incomplete at 0:39. Marshall +3 holders got to enjoy the kneel-down.

The over at 64.5 never had a prayer. It was 6-6 at halftime, and the kickers did the under two big favors after the break: Davis Little missed from 45 late in the third and Jorge Diaz Nicolas missed from 27 early in the fourth. Even with a touchdown called back and two late scores, the game finished with 33 points, 31.5 under.

Card line: New Mexico State −3, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had Sam Houston +3 and the Over, projecting New Mexico State 24, Sam Houston 23. Final: New Mexico State 30, Sam Houston 24. New Mexico State won by 6, and the teams scored 54 points.

New Mexico State −3 needed a four-point win, and the Aggies had a 24-17 lead late in the third. Then the break: a Sam Houston lateral to Ishmel Atkins was fumbled and recovered by New Mexico State, and TJ Washington Jr. ran it in from 7 yards out at 0:33 for 30-17. Sam Houston turned it over on downs at 9:54 of the fourth, got the ball right back on an interception by Railyn Adams, and cashed it in with MJ Dowdy's 1-yard touchdown at 4:00 for 30-24. Now the −3 ticket was one Sam Houston touchdown from losing everything. James Jones broke a 30-yard run on the next possession, and New Mexico State never gave the ball back.

The over 44.5 didn't need any of that drama. Washington's touchdown took the total to 47 with a full quarter to play, and Dowdy's touchdown pushed it to 54. The missed extra point after Washington's run didn't matter to anybody's ticket, which is the nicest thing you can say about a missed extra point.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Sam Houston +3, missed by 3 points. Follow The Money on the Under 44.5, went over by 9.5 points.

Card line: James Madison −10.5, total 56.5. The Cover Writer's card had James Madison −10.5 and the Under, projecting James Madison 35, App State 20. Final in overtime: James Madison 31, App State 34. App State won by 3, and the teams scored 65 points.

James Madison −10.5 needed 11, and the Dukes never got there. They led 21-13 late in the third after Camden Coleman's 19-yard touchdown pass to Cole Keller, and App State tied it early in the fourth with a touchdown and a two-point conversion. Tied 24-24 with six minutes left, Coleman was intercepted by Colton Phares, and moments later Henry Hasselbeck threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Luke Douglas for a 31-24 App State lead. Coleman tied it with a 6-yard touchdown run at 0:03, which saved James Madison's hopes of winning and did nothing for anybody laying the points. In overtime Morgan Suarez missed from 47 and James London won it from 40.

The over is where this game lived. At 24-24 with six minutes left there were 48 points on the board, and Hasselbeck's touchdown made it 55, a point and a half short of the 56.5. Then Coleman's touchdown with three seconds left in regulation took it to 62. If you had the under, you lost it on a 6-yard run with three ticks on the clock, which is about as backdoor as a total gets. Overtime added three more for good measure.
Called it: Next Man Up on the Over 56.5, cleared it by 8.5 points.

Card line: Liberty −11.5, total 49.5. The Cover Writer's card had Kennesaw State +11.5 and the Under, projecting Liberty 28, Kennesaw State 18. Final: Liberty 34, Kennesaw State 6. Liberty won by 28, and the teams scored 40 points.

Kennesaw State +11.5 backers went to halftime down 14-3, which is about as live as a dog ticket gets. Then the Owls handed the third quarter away. They threw interceptions to Derrell Farrar and Ashton McShane, Jaylon Coleman ran 9 yards for a 24-3 lead at 1:37, and a fourth-down stop came on the very next series. Terron Kellman's 2-yard touchdown run in the fourth made it 34-3, and the Liberty −11.5 crowd could stop checking the score.

The under 49.5 cashed without a sweat. The last points came on Daniel Kinney's 28-yard field goal with 1:11 left, the kind of late kick that usually only matters to the total. It didn't matter here either. The game ended with 40 points, 9.5 to spare. Kennesaw State +11.5 needed points, and two third-quarter interceptions made it hard to get them.

Card line: Memphis −10, total 54.5. The Cover Writer's card had Memphis −10 and the Under, projecting Memphis 33, East Carolina 21. Final in overtime: East Carolina 34, Memphis 41. Memphis won by 7, and the teams scored 75 points.

Memphis −10 holders went to halftime down 16-3, which is not how you draw it up. Marcus Stokes dragged them back, and his 2-yard touchdown run with 3:31 left made it 34-27 Memphis. That was still three short of the number, and Mitch Griffis answered with a 20-yard touchdown pass to Landon Sides at 1:30 to tie it anyway. In overtime Stokes ran 5 yards for the go-ahead touchdown, and from there the only way a −10 ticket cashes is a defensive score. Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted Griffis in the end zone, and it went for a touchback. Memphis won by 7, and East Carolina +10 holders cashed on a team that lost.

The over 54.5 had its own sweat. Stokes's 4-yard touchdown pass at 9:48 of the fourth tied it 27-27, and that left the total at 54, half a point short, for more than six minutes. Stokes's run with 3:31 left finally took it to 61, and overtime pushed it to 75.

Missed: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on Memphis −10, missed by 3 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 54.5, went over by 20.5 points.

Card line: Virginia −1.5, total 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had Virginia −1.5 and the Over, projecting Virginia 25, Duke 23. Final: Duke 19, Virginia 16. Duke won by 3, and the teams scored 35 points.

Virginia −1.5 only needed the Cavaliers to win, and with 3:00 left they were winning. Will Bettridge's 30-yard field goal made it 16-13, and the −1.5 crowd started counting. Duke answered with 1:14 to go when Nate Sheppard threw a 28-yard touchdown pass to Brody Keefe for a 19-16 lead, and Patrick Smith-Young intercepted Beau Pribula at 0:43. Virginia backers will be thinking about the 47-yarder Bettridge missed in the third quarter for a while. Duke +1.5 holders won the ticket and the game.

Under 46.5 holders had the easiest night of anybody. The game had 26 points with nine minutes left, and even a field goal and a touchdown in the last three minutes only got it to 35. Duke took a knee at 0:10 to finish it, and the under won by 11.5.

Card line: UConn −15.5, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had Massachusetts +15.5 and the Over, projecting UConn 33, Massachusetts 21. Final: Massachusetts 16, UConn 35. UConn won by 19, and the teams scored 51 points.

UConn −15.5 holders were sitting pretty at 28-3 after Shamar Porter returned a blocked punt for a touchdown in the third. Massachusetts got a touchdown back early in the fourth, and Kalieb Osborne's 13-yard run made it 35-9 at 3:04. Then came the late score that had everybody checking the math. Justin Williams-Thomas's 6-yard touchdown run with 1:09 left made it 35-16, a 19-point game. That left the Huskies 3.5 points clear of the number, so Massachusetts +15.5 got the backdoor open and couldn't walk through it.

That same touchdown decided the total, and it was a gut punch for the under. After Osborne's run the game sat at 44 points, 4.5 short of the 48.5, and the under crowd needed to survive 3:04. Williams-Thomas scored with 1:09 left and took it to 51. Garbage time is never garbage for somebody holding a total.

Card line: Army −1.5, total 53.5. The Cover Writer's card had Army −1.5 and the Under, projecting Army 28, Tulsa 24. Final: Army 38, Tulsa 35. Army won by 3, and the teams scored 73 points.

Army −1.5 was dead and buried, and then it got dug up. Tulsa led 35-28 after Baylor Hayes' 13-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth. At 8:31 Hayes hit C. Gacayan for what would have been a two-score lead, and a Tulsa holding flag wiped it out. Tulsa's Owen Carey then missed from 40. With four minutes left Tim Kloska blocked a Tulsa punt and recovered it at the Tulsa 13, Cale Hellums tied it with a 1-yard run at 1:50, and Dawson Jones kicked a 50-yard field goal on the final play. Army won by 3 and covered by 1.5, and Tulsa +1.5 holders learned that a field goal at the gun beats a hook just fine.

The total was settled in the third quarter. Tulsa's Trequan Jones ran 59 yards for a touchdown that tied it 28-28, and that was 56 points, already past the 53.5. Under holders got to watch the wild finish as neutral fans, which is a polite way of saying they had nothing left to root for.

Missed: The Formula on Tulsa +1.5, missed by 1.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under 53.5, went over by 19.5 points.

Card line: Air Force −5.5, total 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had Air Force −5.5 and the Under, projecting Air Force 26, Wyoming 19. Final: Air Force 14, Wyoming 28. Wyoming won by 14, and the teams scored 42 points.

Air Force −5.5 needed a comeback and then some. Down 21-14 early in the fourth, K. Hodges ran 11 yards for what would have been the tying touchdown, and an Air Force holding flag erased it. On its next two drives Josh Johnson lost fumbles, first forced by Gary Rutherford and then by Ja'Quan Redfern. Wyoming's Markell Holman scored from a yard out at 3:04 for the 28-14 final. Wyoming +5.5 holders won outright and never had to sweat a second-half Air Force lead, because there wasn't one.

The under 45.5 was the quiet winner. The game had 35 points with a quarter to play, and the flag on Hodges took a touchdown off the board. Holman's touchdown put it at 42, 3.5 under, and the under crowd owes a thank-you note to whoever threw that flag.

Called it: Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on Wyoming +5.5, covered by 19.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under 45.5, stayed under by 3.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and The Formula on Air Force −5.5, missed by 19.5 points. Follow The Money on the Over 45.5, fell 3.5 points short.

Card line: NC State −7, total 55.5. The Cover Writer's card had NC State −7 and the Over, projecting NC State 33, Stanford 25. Final: NC State 28, Stanford 31. Stanford won by 3, and the teams scored 59 points.

NC State −7 needed better than a touchdown at Stanford and spent the second half trailing. A 47-yard CJ Bailey touchdown pass to E. Dowdy early in the third came back on a penalty, and Davis Warren answered with a 5-yard touchdown pass for 28-14 Stanford. Emmet Kenney's 31-yard field goal at 8:27 made it 31-21, and Bailey's 16-yard touchdown pass to Keenan Jackson with 1:20 left got it to 31-28. Stanford then went to the kneel-down, NC State got flagged for illegal substitution during the first one, and Warren knelt three more times. The Wolfpack lost outright, and −7 missed by 10.

Over 55.5 holders were stuck at 52 after Kenney's kick with 8:27 left, needing one more score from anybody. Bailey's touchdown with 1:20 left took it to 59, and the over cashed. Stanford's kneel-downs kept it right there, which was fine by everyone holding the over.

Card line: LSU −7, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Auburn +7 and the Under, projecting LSU 28, Auburn 22. Final: LSU 38, Auburn 17. LSU won by 21, and the teams scored 55 points.

Auburn +7 holders were done by halftime. Sam Leavitt threw a 70-yard touchdown pass to Jackson Harris at 4:29 for 24-10, then ran one in himself from 4 yards out at 0:17 for 31-10. LSU −7 cashed comfortably, and nothing after the break made it closer than three touchdowns.

The over 50.5 was the real ballgame. Dilin Jones's 12-yard touchdown run early in the fourth made it 38-10 and 48 points, 2.5 short of the over, and then nobody scored for 13 minutes. Auburn turned it over on downs at 4:20. With 29 seconds left Auburn had a touchdown catch wiped out by a penalty, and every over ticket in the country groaned. Five seconds later Tristan Ti'a ran 7 yards for the touchdown at 0:24. That made it 38-17 and 55 points, over by 4.5. Late points in a blowout are where over tickets get saved, and this one got saved.

Card line: Tennessee −1.5, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Tennessee −1.5 and the Over, projecting Tennessee 29, South Carolina 27. Final: Tennessee 24, South Carolina 27. South Carolina won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

Tennessee was a 1.5-point road favorite, so the Vols just had to win by two. South Carolina led 14-0 after LaNorris Sellers ran 31 yards for a touchdown, but Tennessee came back, and late in the third Sellers was sacked on fourth down with Tennessee up 21-17. Early in the fourth George MacIntyre hit Braylon Staley for an 18-yard touchdown, and a flag wiped it out. Tennessee settled for Cooper Ranvier's 37-yard field goal and a 24-17 lead. With 3:35 left MacIntyre was stopped on fourth down at the South Carolina 39. Sellers ran 4 yards to tie it at 1:17. Then Dylan Stewart sacked MacIntyre and forced a fumble, and Tomiwa Durojaiye recovered at 0:33. Malik Orsan kicked a 48-yard field goal on the final play. Tennessee went from up seven with 3:35 left to a 3-point loss, and −1.5 missed by 4.5.

The over/under was 50.5, and this one went down to the final snap. Ranvier's field goal made it 41, and the flag on the Staley touchdown kept it there. Sellers's run made it 48, still 2.5 short. Orsan's 48-yarder at the gun made it 51. The over cashed by half a point on the last kick of the night.

Card line: Oklahoma −2.5, total 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had Mississippi State +2.5 and the Over, projecting Oklahoma 25, Mississippi State 24. Final: Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 15. Oklahoma won by 8, and the teams scored 38 points.

Oklahoma was laying 2.5 on the road, and Mississippi State +2.5 needed a lot of things to go right. Tate Sandell's 30-yard field goal made it 20-7 Oklahoma late in the third. Mississippi State turned it over on downs at 1:24 of the third and again at 13:03 of the fourth. Then Peyton Bowen intercepted Parker Puckett at the Oklahoma goal line at 8:07. Sandell's 38-yarder made it 23-7 at 4:26. Puckett's 42-yard touchdown pass to Sanfrisco Magee and the two-point conversion at 2:10 made it 23-15, and Oklahoma was kneeling by 0:58. Oklahoma won by 8, so −2.5 covered by 5.5.

The over/under was 46.5, and the under owes Sandell a fruit basket. He missed from 45 twice. His 36-yard make was wiped out by an Oklahoma illegal formation penalty, and he missed the 41-yard retry. The game finished at 38.

Alabama was laying 14.5 at home, so Texas A&M +14.5 got to sweat the whole fourth quarter. Dijon Lee Jr. returned a Marcel Reed interception 39 yards for an Alabama touchdown early, but Reed ran 4 yards for a 14-10 A&M lead in the second quarter, and David Olano's 25-yard field goal made it 20-17 A&M in the third. The over/under was 51.5. Edwards's touchdown made it 51 with 10 minutes left, half a point under. Conor Talty had missed from 36 and 42, and those two kneel-downs inside the 20 were the under's best friends. Half a point under.

Texas was laying 3.5 at home and led 24-3 in the second quarter after Michael Terry III's 2-yard run. Then Ole Miss stormed back. Arch Manning was sacked for a 23-yard loss, and Ole Miss recovered his fumble in the end zone for a touchdown. Trinidad Chambliss threw touchdown passes of 6 and 27 yards to Horatio Fields, and it was 24-24 at 13:57 of the fourth. Manning was intercepted on the next drive, but he scored on a 1-yard run at 8:04 for 31-24. Ole Miss's 58-yard field goal try was blocked by Alex January, and Gianni Spetic's 33-yarder at 2:25 made it 34-24. Lucas Carneiro's 39-yarder made it 34-27 at 1:22. Then Jelani McDonald intercepted Chambliss in the end zone at 0:02. A touchdown there would have tied it and put Ole Miss +3.5 back on the right side of the number. Texas won by 7, so −3.5 covered by 3.5.
The over/under was 52.5. Fields's tying touchdown made it 48, and Manning's touchdown made it 55. The game finished at 61.

Adam Zouagui made field goals from 47 and 32 yards for 27-17, still 1.5 short. Ty Bryant intercepted Jared Curtis, and a Vanderbilt pass interference penalty at the goal line set up Kenny Minchey's 1-yard run at 5:11 for 34-17. Kentucky won by 17, so −11.5 covered by 5.5.

Card line: Indiana −7, total 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had Indiana −7 and the Over, projecting Indiana 28, Michigan 16. Final in overtime: Indiana 13, Michigan 6. Indiana won by 7, and the teams scored 19 points.

Indiana −7 is a number that lands on a touchdown, and this one landed there in overtime. Indiana led 6-0 at halftime, and Michigan tied it on a 26-yard Trey Butkowski field goal on the final play of regulation. In overtime Josh Hoover ran 4 yards for the touchdown, and the extra point made it 13-6. Michigan's Tommy Carr threw incomplete on fourth down to end it. Indiana won by exactly 7, so every side ticket on this game got its money back, which after four quarters and an overtime like that is honestly a gift. A push in overtime. All that defense and the ticket came back exactly where it started.

The under 41.5 never broke a sweat. Three missed field goals kept the board quiet: Butkowski from 53 and 32, and Indiana's Paddy McAteer from 56. The game finished at 19 points, and even overtime only added seven.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over 41.5, fell 22.5 points short.

Card line: Northwestern −16.5, total 58.5. The Cover Writer's card had Northwestern −16.5 and the Under, projecting Northwestern 37, Rutgers 19. Final: Rutgers 14, Northwestern 42. Northwestern won by 28, and the teams scored 56 points.

Northwestern −16.5 holders were up 28-6 and cruising until Rutgers got a 46-yard Antwan Raymond touchdown run and a two-point conversion at 0:08 of the third. That made it 28-14, a 14-point game, and a losing ticket with a quarter to go. Aidan Chiles fixed it himself with a 4-yard touchdown pass to Drew Wagner and a 37-yard touchdown run at 4:33 for 42-14. paragraphs: Same rules as Part 1: card line at kickoff, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Here is how the week came out for everybody, in the usual card order.

The Cover Writer went 25-30-1 against the spread and 25-31 on totals. The push was Indiana at Michigan, 13-6 in overtime, which landed exactly on the number. The Cover Writer would like the record to show that overtime was not on the card.
The Formula went 26-29-1 on sides and 26-30 on totals. The arithmetic was fine. The football just declined to cooperate.
Next Man Up went 26-29-1 on sides and 27-29 on totals. It did a little better on the totals than on the sides, and it plans to keep doing the reading this week.
Letdown Watch went 28-27-1 on sides and 28-28 on totals. That is a winning week on sides, and Letdown Watch has already been reminded that a good Saturday is how a letdown starts.
Follow The Money went 14-16 on sides and 20-14 on totals, picking only when the number moved. When the money talked on totals, it mostly told the truth.
In The Trenches went 12-12 on sides and 8-16 on totals. The sides broke even. The totals are being sent back to the line of scrimmage for more film work.

Now the smack talk for Halloween Saturday. The early number has Ohio State −7 at USC with a total of 52.5, and that one should start a few friendly arguments. The Georgia-Florida game has Georgia −10.5 and a 56.5 total, and the only thing scarier than that spread is whoever has to pick against it. Notre Dame and Navy meet at Gillette Stadium with Notre Dame −30.5 on the board. Whoever loses that argument this week owes the group chat a sincere apology and a bag of candy.
